svg.text: BEST FOR: DETERMINISTIC CITATION CHECK + JEV LOOP
FORMAT LINEAGE: Sumanth P (#04, 124 likes) • LangChain Deep Agents + JEV + Tavily + LangSmith
Deep Research Agent with Deterministic Citation Verification and a Bounded JEV Review Loop
Never ship a research report just because an LLM formatted citations nicely — verify URLs & quote spans in Python, then run a 1-retry JEV gate.
END-TO-END DEEP RESEARCH & DETERMINISTIC + JEV VERIFICATION ARCHITECTURE
RESEARCH_AGAIN (MAX 1 TARGETED RETRY WITH MISSING-EVIDENCE QUERIES)
Passes exact unsupported claims + failed URL spans back to Stage 02 so the agent repairs only what failed.
WHY NAIVE RESEARCH AGENTS FAIL IN PRODUCTION
The URL is real, but the linked paragraph says nothing about
the number claimed in the sentence.
When Source A says 14% and Source B says 42%, naive prompts
pick one and hide the conflict.
Without a hard retry cap (max_retries=1), self-reflecting
Every cited URL must exist in the session's
fetched_sources[] table — zero unvisited links allowed.
Verify exact_quote_span appears in the cached document text
Every percentage, dollar figure, or benchmark score in prose
must appear in its linked span.
Block denylisted low-trust domains and flag sources older
STAGE 05: JEV GATE & BOUNDED RETRY CONTRACT
Targeted delta search (not a full restart)
On RESEARCH_AGAIN, Stage 02 runs only the 2-3 missing-
evidence queries keeping valid sections intact.
If a claim still lacks evidence after 1 targeted retry,
Every search query, deterministic span check, and JEV
verdict is logged to LangSmith / OpenTelemetry.
Rule: Verify URLs and quote spans with deterministic code first; use the LLM judge (JEV) only to grade semantic support and trigger at most 1 retry.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
